big: Zara buys at 10 am and sells at 2 pm, the same day. Sanjay buys the same share and keeps it for five years. Same company, but two very different risks.

lines: Many people say intraday is the way to make quick money. Is it?
It is the way to make quick losses for most people. Short-term prices move randomly, costs add up each trade, and there is no time for a business to grow. Education only, not advice.

rows: Shares go to your demat account, and you keep them as long as you like
Opened and closed the same day, with no delivery
An index of 50 large NSE companies. You cannot buy it directly
Spreading money so one failure does not sink the whole portfolio
note: Index funds and ETFs let you hold an index. The index itself cannot be bought.

title: Risk basics
stops: A delivery trade puts shares in your demat account
Intraday trading is a safe way to make quick profits
The Nifty 50 tracks 50 large NSE companies
Putting all your money in one share is well diversified
caps: Delivery means the shares are yours to hold for as long as you wish.
Intraday trades can lose money fast, and costs add up each day.
The Nifty 50 is a benchmark of the market's direction.
One share means one failure can hurt the whole portfolio.

q: Rohan buys a share on Monday and keeps it for five years. What kind of trade is this?
why: Intraday means opened and closed on the same day, which is not the case.
A stop-loss is an order type, not a way of holding shares.
Shares taken into the demat account and held are a delivery trade.
A bonus is a corporate action and not a type of trade.

q: Meena says the Nifty 50 rose 1% today. What does this mean?
why: The Nifty 50 tracks 50 large listed companies, and it showed a rise of 1%.
An index is a benchmark, so her own holdings can move differently.
Shares do not all move the same way on a given day.
SEBI regulates the market and does not raise it.

q: Rohan puts his whole savings in one company. Which risk is greatest?
opts: SEBI will cancel his demat account
why: The index keeps moving whatever Rohan holds or sells.
With one share, a single failure hits everything he owns.
SEBI does not cancel a demat account over holdings.
The gap between bid and ask is a market feature, and it does not vanish.

opts: Only the share that rose most last week
Only the share a friend recommended
why: Twelve shares of one bank still depend on one sector.
Chasing last week's winner is not a spread of risk.
A friend's tip is a single bet, and not a spread.
Spreading across sectors lowers the harm from one failure.

pts: Delivery means holding shares in your demat account. Intraday closes the same day.
The Nifty 50 tracks 50 large companies. You cannot buy it directly.
Spread your money, so that one failure does not sink the portfolio.
